issues.note: The card drills the four-value enumeration as a closed set. CURRENT-DOCS-DELTA_v1 D1... (D2 entry) states: "Current docs: seven - adds pause_turn (server-tool loop iteration limit), refusal, model_context_window_exceeded" and gives the binding instruction "the generator may mention them but must not mark a 'four values exist' option as correct." The front's hedge ("the corpus defines") softens this but a learner drilling it retrieves "there are four." Keep the four for exam purposes; make the closed-set framing explicit rather than implicit.

suggested.text: `end_turn`, `tool_use`, `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence` - the four the exam guide works from; the loop decision only ever turns on `tool_use` vs `end_turn`.

issues.note: Back says the model "sets `stop_reason` to `tool_use`". The corpus never attributes the setting of `stop_reason` to the model - Domain-1_v2 §1.1 says only "The orchestrator inspects `stop_reason` after each call" and "`tool_use` | Claude wants to call a tool". It also contradicts this deck's own d1-010, whose back reads "`stop_reason` is set by the API on every response". One of the two is wrong; d1-010 matches the corpus framing better.

suggested.text: The model: it emits `tool_use` blocks and the response comes back with `stop_reason: "tool_use"`. The orchestrator's code carries out what was requested.

issues.note: Primary cite is Key-Distinctions_v1 #7, which does not contain the claim. #7 reads in full: "When all subagents succeed but output is incomplete/wrong-domain -> coordinator's task decomposition, not subagent capability. Research system finds only visual art content even though subagents work correctly -> coordinator decomposed into visual art subtasks only. Fix the coordinator prompt, not the subagents." It never names query quality or document filters. The enumeration the back gives lives only in the second cite, Domain-1_v2 §1.6: "Not: web-search agent query quality, synthesis agent gap detection, document analysis filters". Swap the cite order.

The front asks for "two explanations" the exam rules out; Domain-1_v2 §1.6 rules out three ("web-search agent query quality, synthesis agent gap detection, document analysis filters"). Dropping synthesis-agent gap detection is arbitrary and leaves the learner with an incomplete ruled-out set. d1-037 already asks for all three correctly.

suggested.text: Complete-looking subagent output plus missing coverage: which three explanations does the exam rule out?

issues.note: Same question as d1-037 ("Which three components are NOT the root cause?", back: "The web-search agent's query quality, the synthesis agent's gap detection, and the document-analysis filters"). Corrected as above it becomes an exact duplicate; kill it and keep d1-037.

Duplicates d1-004. d1-004 back: "On `end_turn` it stops and returns the output to the user; on `tool_use` it runs the requested tool and issues another API call." d1-093 back: "`tool_use`: execute the requested tool, append the result, call the API again. `end_turn`: stop the loop and return the response to the user." Same fact, same angle, same two cites (§1.1 + Key-Distinctions #5) in swapped order. d1-004's scenario framing is the stronger of the two.

Duplicates d1-003 (text-matching for a completion phrase, answer `stop_reason`), same cites. The only added content is the hang symptom. Either merge that symptom into d1-003 and kill this, or re-angle the front onto something d1-003 does not cover - e.g. why an already-finished turn keeps looping.

Overlaps d1-005 ("Where do tool results go in the next API request of an agentic loop?" / "Appended to `messages` as `tool_result` blocks"). The one fact this card adds beyond d1-005 is `id` matching, which is correctly supported by the second cite (Domain-2_v2 §2.1: "Key fields: `id` (for matching to `tool_result`)"). Keep one card, not both - preferably this one, and retire d1-005.

Overlaps d1-019, which asks the same thing as a scenario ("Which two properties of the intended architecture were given up?" / "Central visibility and uniform error handling") on the same cites. This card adds only the third property, information control. Fold that into d1-019 and drop one.

Duplicates d1-017. d1-017: "A synthesis subagent produces a report missing everything the web-search subagent found... Put the search agent's findings into the synthesis subagent's prompt; isolated context means nothing is inherited automatically." d1-099 asks the same question about the same two agents and gives the same answer. d1-016 also already carries the isolation rule.

The answer (coordinator prompt, partition the research space before delegating) is already carried by d1-036 (fault sits in the coordinator's decomposition) and d1-039 ("Partition the research space in the coordinator before delegating, rather than deduplicating results afterwards"), both on Domain-1_v2 §1.6. Re-angle or drop.

Inverse framing of d1-056, which asks which coordinator options a bare failure status made impossible and answers "Retrying with a modified query, continuing on partial results, and rerouting to an alternative source". Same fact from Key-Distinctions #8 / §1.9. Keep one.

Duplicates d1-052 outright. d1-052: "Name the four parts of the error payload a failing subagent returns." / "Failure type, what was attempted, any partial results, and potential alternatives." d1-102: "What four things does a failing subagent put in the error it returns to its coordinator?" / "Failure type, what was attempted, any partial results, and the alternatives worth trying." Identical enumeration, identical cite pair.

Duplicates d1-022 ("A coordinator never delegates and attempts every task itself... Whether `\"Task\"` is present in its `allowedTools`"), including the same trap about rewriting the system prompt. Only cosmetic difference: `allowed_tools` vs `allowedTools` - the corpus uses both (§1.3 Python snippet vs §1.3 prose "A coordinator's `allowedTools` must include `\"Task\"`"), so neither is wrong, but shipping both spellings in near-identical cards will read as a distinction that does not exist.

Duplicates d1-079. d1-079: "Emitting all the `Task` calls in a single coordinator response; issuing them across separate turns runs them sequentially." d1-105: "The multiple `Task` calls are emitted in a single response. Issued across separate turns they run one after another." Same sentence from §1.15, reworded.

Triple overlap: the stem duplicates d1-072 (human agents re-asking for details already collected) and the back duplicates d1-070's field list ("Customer ID, root-cause analysis, the refund amount, and the recommended action"). Its trap is verbatim the same point as d1-072's trap about raw transcript access.

Its trap field ("resuming the same named session twice continues one accumulating history, so the second evaluation sees the first's conclusions") is the whole answer to d1-085, which asks exactly that question ("Why not run both in a single session, one after the other?"). Drilling this card first hands over d1-085.
Third card on one §1.16 scenario alongside d1-084 (what `fork_session` gives over two fresh sessions) and d1-085. Two is enough.

Duplicates d1-089 ("A second independent instance reviews the changes without seeing the first instance's reasoning") and its trap duplicates d1-090's (extended thinking / self-review instructions keep the same anchored instance). All three sit on Domain-1_v2 §1.17.

Duplicates d1-043. d1-043: "'Add tests across a legacy codebase.' Which decomposition strategy fits?" / "Dynamic adaptive: map the structure first, prioritize high-risk modules, then revise the plan as dependencies surface." d1-109 restates both front and back with no added fact, on the same cite.

Third card on the same distinction as d1-076 ("Where is security-critical sequencing enforced?") and d1-077 ("What makes a prompt instruction the weaker mechanism for mandatory ordering?"), with d1-075 and d1-078 already carrying the scenario form. Five cards on Key-Distinctions #11 / §1.14 is more than the distinction holds.
